 Alex Martin USA TODAY Nov. 5, 2026, 1:29 p.m. ET Hear this story Five-star wide receiver Brysen Wright has committed to the University of Miami for the 2028 recruiting class.
 Wright is ranked as the No. 3 overall prospect in the 2028 class by the 247Sports Composite.
 Wright however is reclassifying from the 2028 class to the 2027 class, something fellow Miami commit A'mir Sears is also doing this year.
 Miami football has landed one of the nation's top offensive prospects in what's been an incredible year for the Hurricanes on the recruiting trail.
 Jacksonville (Florida) Mandarin five-star wide receiver Brysen Wright announced his commitment to the Hurricanes on Thursday, Nov. 5. Wright, a member of USA TODAY Sports preseason All-America team, chose Miami over several national programs, giving coach Mario Cristobal a major addition.
 The 6-foot-3.5, 215-pound receiver also announced other massive news, as he'll be reclassifying from the 2028 class to the 2027 class , something A'mir Sears also did earlier this year after committing to Miami. Both USA TODAY Sports’ latest composite and 247Sports’ composite ranked Wright as the No. 3 overall player in the 2028 class.
 Hurricanes land elite in-state playmaker
 Miami's pursuit of Wright has been bolstered by its early relationship with the Mandarin standout and the opportunity to remain close to home.
 High School Sports: The best preps coverage in the country, from rankings, scores and stats to local and national news—every team matters. The Hurricanes were the first program to offer Wright, and Miami's coaching staff has continued to prioritize him throughout his recruitment.
 Wright also has a connection to Miami through Mandarin quarterback Knox Annis, who committed to the Hurricanes in April. Miami wide receiver Malachi Toney has also publicly recruited Wright, making a pitch for the five-star prospect to join him in Coral Gables.
 Wright brings impressive production to Miami
 Wright has backed up his five-star status with three productive varsity seasons at Mandarin.
 As a freshman in 2024, he recorded 31 receptions for 646 yards and eight touchdowns. He followed that with 46 catches for 983 yards and 10 touchdowns as a sophomore in 2025. Through 10 games of his junior season, Wright has recorded 46 receptions for 984 yards and 11 touchdowns, adding 26 tackles, 2 interceptions and 2 fumble recoveries on defense.
 With Wright committed, the Hurricanes have secured one of the premier wide receiver prospects in the 2027 class and further strengthened their efforts to keep elite in-state talent in Florida.
